instructions: Read the passage and choose one answer for each question.
passage:
On Monday, Mei moves into a small apartment in the fictional town of Brookside. Before unpacking, she and the building manager, Alex, make a maintenance list. Mei notices a damp patch near the kitchen sink. Alex checks the record and explains that a pipe under the sink was inspected last week. A qualified worker will return on Wednesday to find out why the area is still damp. Mei does not try to fix the pipe herself.

The faucet above the sink also drips after it is closed. Mei's friend calls it a tap, the usual British word for a faucet. Alex adds it to the list, together with the drain, which is slow to empty. Mei asks for the visit time in writing because she works from home on Wednesday. Alex says the worker is expected between ten and eleven, but the office will call if the appointment changes.

In the living room, there is a small crack near the top of the wall. The roof was checked after a storm, and Alex has already asked a specialist to look at the new mark. Mei moves a light curtain away from the crack and leaves the carpet where it is. Mei takes a photograph of the crack for the report so that the worker can compare the mark with the photograph later. The photograph is not used to guess the cause.

The handle on a cupboard is loose. A carpenter will inspect its hinge and decide whether to tighten a screw or replace the screw. Alex shows Mei an old bolt that was removed from another cupboard during an earlier job. A hammer and a nail were used to mend a wooden picture frame last month; this time a drill may be needed for a different task. Nobody begins work before the carpenter has checked what is suitable.

Near the entrance, Mei points out that a light bulb is not working. Mei also notices a cable beside a socket and asks whether it is safe to use. The manager records the concern and contacts a qualified technician; Mei leaves the cable, switch and wire alone. The front-door lock was replaced yesterday, and two keys are provided to each resident. Alex explains that routine checks are arranged by the office, while residents are asked to report anything unusual.

On Wednesday the worker confirms the sink appointment. The carpenter will come on Friday to examine the cupboard and may need to loosen the old fitting before installing a new one. Mei reads the schedule once more and sends Alex a short message. She is pleased that each issue has an owner and a time for follow-up. The story is fictional; actual work should follow the building's instructions and be done by an appropriately qualified person.
